source_solver: This port on HiGHS 1.15.1 via PuLP 3.3.2 (SCIP 10.0 gives 121719.17286133836, CBC 121719.172). The original notebook code, run unmodified (only the %pip line dropped) with gurobipy 13.0.3 (size-limited pip licence) on 2026-10-02, gives 121719.1728613383 with 131 variables, 116 constraints, 0 integer variables and 734 nonzeros; the notebook prints 121719.17
notes: The optimum is unique, objective and plan: LP ranging over the optimal face leaves every variable within 1e-6, and HiGHS, SCIP and CBC return the same KPIs. Reference plan: no extra housing and no overtime; 22.8 heifer calves raised in Year1 and 11.58 in Year2, none later (236.95 sold); 92.46 dairy cows in Year5; yearly profit 21906.06, 21888.70, 25816.06, 26825.77, 25282.59, as the notebook prints. Same columns, rows (same order, senses and right-hand sides), bounds and objective coefficients as the original (734 nonzeros; coefficients equal to within 1.4e-17 relative), except that the labour rows count hours instead of hundreds of hours: each labour row is the original's times 100, and the overtime column is in hours at 1.20 per hour instead of 120 per hundred hours. Gurobi stores the original's addRange row for the final dairy herd as final dairy cows + RgFinal_dairy_cows = 175 with the range variable in [0, 125]; the port writes that row and column explicitly (final_dairy_cows_headroom, not a measure), which is the 131st variable. Values hard-coded in the original are data here: 1 acre per dairy cow (cow_acres), half of the calves heifers (heifer_calf_share), the 10-year loan behind the objective's (year + 4) repayments still due after the horizon (loan_term_years: due = loan_term_years minus the repayments inside the horizon), and the zero lower bound of Profit, which forbids a loss-making year (min_yearly_profit). Two generalisations change nothing for the published data: an outlay is repaid only for loan_term_years years (all five here), and a crop yield of 0 drops that crop's acre terms instead of dividing by zero. The scoring KPIs are horizon totals: over 685 optimal what-ifs drawn from the repo's generic templates (390 data changes, 295 new limits) they match on HiGHS, SCIP and CBC, and LP ranging over 240 of them finds them unique, while profit_by_year and dairy_cows_by_year have alternative optima once a rule caps a total over several years. Rules on yearly_profit make almost every plan KPI non-unique (40 of 46 such scenarios disagree across solvers), so the task generator, which requires HiGHS and SCIP to agree, usually drops them; only the objective is safe there. Inherited from the original: a crop sale price above its purchase price makes the LP unbounded (buying to resell is unlimited), and the first-year herd is fixed, so a farm too small for it is infeasible.
